newsitem.title: ITALY: Employers' head doesn't see overall Italy recovery.
newsitem.headline: Employers' head doesn't see overall Italy recovery.

text.p: Giorgio Fossa, chairman of the Italian employers' body Confindustria, said the Italian economy has not yet entered a cycle of productive recovery, apart from certain niche sectors which have reversed the trend.
Speaking to reporters at a meeting of local business leaders, Fossa said that 1997 "certainly will not be very positive" with growth of between one and 1.2 percent.

And to reach that figure "growth in the second half of this year will have to be very robust," he said. The government targets 1997 gross domestic product growth of 1.2 percent but Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said last week he saw average growth of between only one and 1.2 percent.
Fossa said, "we haven't yet reached the turning point, the recovery is not yet here apart from in some niche sectors." he did not specify what these were.
